Produces the manuscript's main figures: Fig2 (A-D), Fig3 (A-D), Fig4 (A-C),
Fig5 (A-B), Fig6 (A-C). Section 15 runs the MixSIAR/JAGS mixing model, which
can take a long time - Fig4 and Fig5 depend on its output. Supplementary
figures are produced separately in Supplementary_figures.Rmd.

#1. Load packages and colour palette

```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(Hmisc)
library(ggpubr)
library(googlesheets4)
library(here)
source(here('script','colors.R'))
set.seed(1)  # reproducible geom_text_repel label placement
```

#2. Load data

```{r}
Data  <- read.csv(here('data','Dataset_S1.csv'), fileEncoding = "macintosh")
Data  <- Data %>% filter(!is.na(Sample_ID))  # drop trailing blank rows
humans <- filter(Data, group == "Human")
fauna <- filter(Data, group == "Fauna")
```

#3. Create indices for Fig2/Fig3

```{r}
fauna <-fauna %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(valphe_13C = (c(val_d13C - phe_d13C)))
fauna <-fauna %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(lysphe_15N = (c(lys_d15N - phe_d15N)))
fauna <-fauna %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(gluphe_15N = (c(glu_d15N - phe_d15N)))
humans <-humans %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(valphe_13C = (c(val_d13C - phe_d13C)))
humans <-humans %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(lysphe_15N = (c(lys_d15N - phe_d15N)))
humans <-humans %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(gluphe_15N = (c(glu_d15N - phe_d15N)))
```

Site and faunal-category colours come from script/colors.R (source()'d above):
`category_cols` (fauna-only panels, Fig2a-d) and `combined_cols`/`combined_order`
(panels showing both fauna categories and human sites, Fig3a-d).

#4. Fig2a Bulk isotope values of fauna

```{r}
library(ggrepel)
Fig2a <-ggplot()+
  labs(y=expression(delta^{15}*N[collagen]*"(‰)"), x=expression(delta^{13}*C[collagen]*"(‰)"))+
  scale_x_continuous(position="bottom", limits=c(-25,-5))+
  scale_y_continuous(position = "left", limits=c(0,20))+
 geom_point(data=fauna, aes(y=d15N, x=d13C, fill=category), colour="black", pch=23, alpha=0.6, size=4)+
  geom_text_repel(data=fauna, aes(y=d15N, x=d13C, label=common_name), size=2.1,
                  seed=1, max.overlaps=Inf, box.padding=0.5, point.padding=0.3,
                  force=3, force_pull=0.5, max.time=2, max.iter=1e5,
                  min.segment.length=Inf, segment.size=0.2)+  # never draw a leader line - just place the label near its point
  scale_fill_manual(values=category_cols, breaks=names(category_cols))+
    theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())+
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1)
Fig2a
```

#7. Fig2d faunal remains fingerprinting

Define reference ranges from primary producer databases.

```{r}
Ref_C <-  read.csv(here('data','C_fingerprinting.csv'))
Ref_N <-  read.csv(here('data','N_fingerprinting.csv'))
#select EAA
Ref_C <- Ref_C %>%  dplyr::select(Group, Category, Code, ile_d13C, leu_d13C, lys_d13C, val_d13C, phe_d13C)
Ref_C <-Ref_C %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(valphe_13C = (c(val_d13C - phe_d13C)))
Ref_C <- Ref_C %>% dplyr::filter(Category == 'C3_terrestrial_plant' | Category == 'phytoplankton' |Category == 'green algae' |Category == 'brown algae' |Category == 'red algae')
Ref_C <- na.omit(Ref_C)


Ref_N <- Ref_N %>%  dplyr::select(Group, Group1, Category, Code, phe_d15N, lys_d15N)
Ref_N <-Ref_N %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(lysphe_15N = (c(lys_d15N - phe_d15N)))
# Grouped by the coarser Group1 column (Terrestrial plants / Phytoplankton /
# Macroalgae), which folds red/green/brown algae together under Macroalgae.
# N_fingerprinting.csv's Code is keyed to Group1, while C_fingerprinting.csv's
# Code (used below for Ref_C_labels) is keyed to the finer Category column.
Ref_N <- Ref_N %>% dplyr::filter(Group1 %in% c('Macroalgae', 'Phytoplankton', 'Terrestrial plants'))
Ref_N <- na.omit(Ref_N) #

# Short Code labels (e.g. "TP", "Phyto", "BA") for each reference category,
# used to label the density curves in the Fig2d/Fig3d marginal panels.
#
# find_exclusive_label_pos() places each label where its curve is tallest
# relative to the others, landing it in a section of the distribution that
# isn't buried under a neighbouring category, rather than at the raw peak
# (which can sit in a heavily overlapping zone). Falls back to a category's
# own peak if it is never the tallest anywhere.
find_exclusive_label_pos <- function(data, value_col, group_col, grid) {
  groups <- unique(data[[group_col]])
  dens_mat <- sapply(groups, function(g) {
    vals <- data[[value_col]][data[[group_col]] == g]
    d <- density(vals)
    approx(d$x, d$y, xout = grid, rule = 2)$y
  })
  dominant <- groups[max.col(dens_mat, ties.method = "first")]
  out <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i) {
    g <- groups[i]
    idx <- which(dominant == g)
    if (length(idx) == 0) {
      # never the tallest curve anywhere - fall back to this category's own peak
      x_pos <- grid[which.max(dens_mat[, i])]
    } else {
      runs <- split(idx, cumsum(c(1, diff(idx) != 1)))
      best_run <- runs[[which.max(lengths(runs))]]
      x_pos <- grid[best_run[which.max(dens_mat[best_run, i])]]
    }
    y_pos <- 0.5 * approx(grid, dens_mat[, i], xout = x_pos)$y
    data.frame(group = g, peak_x = x_pos, peak_y = y_pos)
  })
  setNames(do.call(rbind, out), c(group_col, "peak_x", "peak_y"))
}

grid_C <- seq(-6, 9, length.out = 600)   # matches Ref_C_plot's display window
Ref_C_labels <- find_exclusive_label_pos(Ref_C, "valphe_13C", "Category", grid_C) %>%
  left_join(distinct(Ref_C, Category, Code), by = "Category")

# Same idea for the y-axis (Nitrogen) marginal density, labelled by Group1's
# own Code (MA/Phyto/TP).
grid_N <- seq(-11, 6, length.out = 600)  # matches Ref_N_plot's display window
Ref_N_labels <- find_exclusive_label_pos(Ref_N, "lysphe_15N", "Group1", grid_N) %>%
  left_join(distinct(Ref_N, Group1, Code), by = "Group1")

# Display-only copies of Ref_C/Ref_N, restricted to a window a little wider
# than Fig2d_base's own axis limits. Keeps the density curves from being
# dominated by far-outlying reference values without needing a
# coord_cartesian()/coord_flip() on xdens/ydens (which would break their
# alignment with Fig2d_base).
Ref_C_plot <- Ref_C %>% dplyr::filter(valphe_13C >= -6, valphe_13C <= 9)
Ref_N_plot <- Ref_N %>% dplyr::filter(lysphe_15N >= -11, lysphe_15N <= 6)
```

Reference producer category colours come from script/colors.R (`ref_cols` /
`ref_group1_cols`).

Make base plot for Fig2d/Fig3d.

```{r}
Fig2d_base <-ggplot() +
  geom_point(data=fauna, aes(y=lysphe_15N,  x=valphe_13C, fill=category), colour="black", pch=23,alpha=0.6, size=4)+
  geom_text_repel(data=fauna, aes(y=lysphe_15N, x=valphe_13C, label=common_name), size=2.1,
                  seed=1, max.overlaps=Inf, box.padding=0.5, point.padding=0.3,
                  force=3, force_pull=0.5, max.time=2, max.iter=1e5,
                  min.segment.length=Inf, segment.size=0.2)+  # never draw a leader line - just place the label near its point
  labs(y=expression(Delta^{15}*N[Lys-Phe]*"(‰)"), x=expression(Delta^{13}*C[Val-Phe]*"(‰)"))+
   scale_fill_manual(values=category_cols, breaks=names(category_cols))+
  scale_x_continuous(position="bottom", limits=c(-5,8))+
  scale_y_continuous(position = "left",limits=c(-10,5))+
  theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())+
  # Legend suppressed here rather than at the outer ggarrange level - a legend
  # baked into this cowplot composite can't be stripped the way a plain
  # ggplot panel's can. Category colours are already shown in Fig2a-c.
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  coord_fixed(ratio = 0.87)
Fig2d_base
```

Make the composite Fig2d/Fig3d "big D" plot (main panel + marginal densities).

```{r}
library (ggExtra)
library(ggpubr)
library(cowplot)
# axis_canvas() aligns xdens/ydens to Fig2d_base's coordinate system.
# Ref_C_plot/Ref_N_plot (filtered above) keep the density curves within the
# visible window, and legend.position="none" avoids a redundant Category
# legend here (already shown via Fig2d_base/the outer figure's legend).
xdens <- axis_canvas(Fig2d_base, axis = "x") +
  geom_density(data= Ref_C_plot, aes(x = valphe_13C, fill = Category), alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.2) +
  # geom_label_repel draws a white box behind each label, coloured/bordered to
  # match its curve (scale_colour_manual(values=ref_cols)) so it's clear which
  # curve each label belongs to. direction="y" keeps each label's x fixed at
  # its own median, so repel only slides labels vertically to dodge
  # collisions rather than drifting onto a neighbouring curve.
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = Ref_C_labels, aes(x = peak_x, y = peak_y, label = Code, colour = Category),
            size = 2.2, fontface = "bold", seed = 1, direction = "y",
            fill = "white", label.size = 0.35, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"),
            force = 2, force_pull = 0.3,
            min.segment.length = Inf, segment.size = 0.2, box.padding = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ref_cols) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ref_cols) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
ydens <- axis_canvas(Fig2d_base, axis = "y", coord_flip = TRUE) +
  geom_density(data = Ref_N_plot, aes(x = lysphe_15N, fill = Group1), alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.2) +
  # Same approach as xdens above; pre-flip this keeps each label's peak_x
  # (its Nitrogen median) fixed so post-flip it stays aligned with the
  # correct point on Fig2d_base's y-axis.
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = Ref_N_labels, aes(x = peak_x, y = peak_y, label = Code, colour = Group1),
            size = 2.2, fontface = "bold", seed = 1, direction = "y",
            fill = "white", label.size = 0.35, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"),
            force = 2, force_pull = 0.3,
            min.segment.length = Inf, segment.size = 0.2, box.padding = 0.25) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ref_group1_cols) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ref_group1_cols) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
# panel_d_scale controls how much extra width/height Fig2d/Fig3d's grid cell
# gets, to offset the marginal density strips' share of the composite. D's
# core plotted area scales as panel_d_scale/(1+margin_frac) relative to
# A/B/C, so setting it to exactly 1+margin_frac makes D's core panel match
# A/B/C's size.
margin_frac <- 0.25  # relative size of the marginal density strip
panel_d_scale <- 1 + margin_frac
Fig2d <- insert_xaxis_grob(Fig2d_base, xdens, grid::unit(margin_frac, "null"), position = "top")
Fig2d <- insert_yaxis_grob(Fig2d, ydens, grid::unit(margin_frac, "null"), position = "right")
Fig2d <-ggdraw(Fig2d)
Fig2d
```

#8. Save Fig2 (A-D)

```{r}
library(ggpubr)
# Fig2d is a cowplot composite (main panel + marginal density strips), so its
# core scatter area would be smaller than a plain panel in the same grid
# cell as Fig2a-c. Arranging rows separately lets Fig2d's cell get the extra
# width/height (panel_d_scale) needed to compensate.
Fig2_top    <- ggarrange(Fig2a, Fig2b, ncol = 2, labels = c("A", "B"), legend = "none")
Fig2_bottom <- ggarrange(Fig2c, Fig2d, ncol = 2, labels = c("C", "D"), legend = "none",
                         widths = c(1, panel_d_scale))
Fig2 <- ggarrange(Fig2_top, Fig2_bottom, nrow = 2, heights = c(1, panel_d_scale))
Fig2
# Scaling the whole canvas by panel_d_scale keeps A/B/C/D in the same
# proportions. The raw scaled size (8.9*(1+panel_d_scale) ~ 20.9cm) exceeds
# Elsevier/JAS's 190mm double-column maximum, so it's capped at 19cm; this
# scales all panels uniformly and doesn't affect font size (set in points).
fig2_side <- min(8.9 * (1 + panel_d_scale), 19)
ggsave(here('figures','Fig2.svg'), width = fig2_side, height = fig2_side, dpi = 300, units = "cm", device='svg')
# Vector PDF for journal submission (Elsevier/JAS accepts EPS or PDF for vector
# figures); cairo_pdf renders the delta/permil Unicode symbols correctly.
ggsave(here('figures','Fig2.pdf'), width = fig2_side, height = fig2_side, dpi = 300, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)
```

#14. Prepare EAA data for the MixSIAR mixing model (Fig4/Fig5)

```{r}
EAA <- Data %>%  dplyr::select(Site, Region, Sample_ID, category, common_name, Group, group, d34S,d13C,d15N, ile_d13C, leu_d13C, lys_d13C, val_d13C, phe_d13C, phe_d15N, lys_d15N)
```

Create a source data file for marine and terrestrial faunal references and
find means and SDs (needed for multiple tracers rather than a 'raw' model).

```{r}
Sources <- EAA %>% subset(group =="Fauna")
Sources <- Sources %>%filter(!common_name == "guinea pig" & !common_name == "armadillo"& !common_name == "coati")

Source_means <- Sources %>% group_by(Group) %>% summarise (Meanile_d13C
 = mean(ile_d13C), Meanleu_d13C  = mean(leu_d13C), Meanlys_d13C
 = mean(lys_d13C), Meanval_d13C = mean(val_d13C), Meanphe_d13C = mean(phe_d13C), Meanphe_d15N = mean(phe_d15N), Meanlys_d15N = mean(lys_d15N), SDile_d13C = sd(ile_d13C), SDleu_d13C  = sd(leu_d13C), SDlys_d13C = sd(lys_d13C), SDval_d13C = sd(val_d13C), SDphe_d13C = sd(phe_d13C), SDphe_d15N = mean(phe_d13C), SDlys_d15N = mean(lys_d15N), n = n())

write.csv (Source_means, here::here("mixingmodel", "Sources.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

Create a consumer data file for human data.

```{r}
Humans <- EAA %>% subset(group =="Human")
write.csv (Humans, here('mixingmodel','Humans.csv'), row.names=FALSE)
```

#15. Apply the MixSIAR model

Load source data and consumer data.

```{r}
library(devtools)
library(MixSIAR)

#Load mixture data
mix <- load_mix_data(filename=here('mixingmodel','Humans.csv'), iso_names=c("ile_d13C", "leu_d13C", "lys_d13C", "val_d13C", "phe_d13C", "phe_d15N", "lys_d15N"),
                     factors="Sample_ID",
                     fac_random=FALSE,
                     fac_nested=FALSE,
                     cont_effects=NULL)

#Load source data
source <- load_source_data(filename=here('mixingmodel','Sources.csv'),
                           source_factors=NULL,
                           conc_dep=FALSE,
                           data_type="means",
                           mix)
#Load discrimination data including the offsets for the EAAs if required. Note d13C lysine does not have a value.
discr <- load_discr_data(filename= here::here("mixingmodel", "Discr.csv"), mix)
```

Create the JAGS file and run the model (test, then the full "very long" run).

```{r}
model_filename <- "MixSIAR_model.txt"# Name of the JAGS model file
resid_err <-FALSE
process_err <-TRUE
write_JAGS_model(model_filename, resid_err, process_err, mix, source)
```

```{r}
jags.1 <- run_model(run="test", mix, source, discr, model_filename)
```

```{r}
jags.1 <- run_model(run="very long", mix, source, discr, model_filename)
```

Get posterior chains into one tidy data frame.

Run diagnostics and create a data frame with summary stats. Check the
console output to make sure the model has converged.

```{r}
diag <- output_diagnostics(jags.1, mix, source, output_options)
head(diag$gelman)
df.stats <- output_stats(jags.1, mix, source, output_options)
rownames(df.stats)
df.stats <- as.data.frame(df.stats)
diag
```

#19. Derive trophic position from % marine mix (Ramirez et al. values)

Derive the terrestrial beta value from herbivores, assuming they are TP2.

```{r}
T_herb <- Data %>%filter(category == "terrestrial_herbivore")
T_herb <- T_herb %>%filter(!common_name == "guinea pig" & !common_name == "armadillo"& !common_name == "coati")
T_herb <-  T_herb %>% rowwise() %>% mutate (beta = 7.6-(glu_d15N-phe_d15N) )
beta_T = mean(T_herb$beta)
sigma_beta_T = sd(T_herb$beta)
beta_T
sigma_beta_T
```

Calculate the uncertainties on trophic level estimates.

```{r}
# ---- Input Data ----
# Measured values
beta_M <- -3.3 #Marine beta value from  Ramirez et al.
beta_T <- 6.6 #Terrestrial beta value from Ramirez et al.
TDF <- 7.6  # Trophic discriminat factor from Ramirez

# Standard deviations from Ramirez
sigma_beta_M <- 1.8 # marine beta uncertainty
sigma_beta_T <- 3.4  # terrestrial beta uncertainty
sigma_TDF <- 1.1 # TDF uncertainty from Neilsen

# Partial derivatives, added to a new sheet
Result_mix_TP <- Result_mix %>% rowwise() %>%
mutate(dTP_dGlu = ((1/TDF)^2)*(glu_d15Nstdev^2))%>%mutate(dTP_dPhe=((-1/TDF)^2)*(phe_d15Nstdev^2))%>%mutate(dTP_dBeta=(((beta_M-beta_T)/TDF)^2)*(SD_marine^2))%>%mutate(dTP_dBeta_T=(((Mean_terrestrial)/TDF)^2)*(sigma_beta_T^2))%>%mutate(dTP_dBeta_M=((Mean_marine/TDF)^2)*(sigma_beta_M^2))%>%mutate(dTP_sigma=(((-1/(TDF^2))*(glu_d15N-phe_d15N+((Mean_terrestrial)*beta_T)+(Mean_marine*beta_M)))^2)*(sigma_TDF^2))
```

```{r}
# Calculate trophic position using Ramirez values and add the combined uncertainty
Result_mix_TP_final <- Result_mix_TP %>%
  rowwise() %>% mutate(Mix_TP = (((glu_d15N - phe_d15N) + (((Mean_marine)*beta_M) + ((Mean_terrestrial))*beta_T)) / TDF) + 1)%>% mutate(Mix_TP_sigma = (sqrt(dTP_dGlu + dTP_dPhe + dTP_dBeta +dTP_dBeta_T + dTP_dBeta_M + dTP_sigma)))
```

#20. Fig4c estimated trophic position against % marine source AA

```{r}
Fig4c <- ggplot(Result_mix_TP_final) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(y=Mix_TP, x=Mean_marine, ymax=(Mix_TP+Mix_TP_sigma), ymin=(Mix_TP-Mix_TP_sigma)), linewidth=0.2)+
  geom_errorbarh(aes(y=Mix_TP, x=Mean_marine, xmax=(Mean_marine+SD_marine),xmin=(Mean_marine-SD_marine)), linewidth=0.2)+
    geom_point(data= Result_mix_TP_final, aes(y=Mix_TP, x= Mean_marine, fill = Site), pch=21, size = 3, colour = "black")+
  scale_fill_manual(values=site_cols, breaks=site_order)+
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1))+
  ylab ("Estimated trophic positon - 'BetaMix'")+
  xlab ("% marine source AA_MixSIAR")+
  geom_hline (yintercept=c(2.04,2.57), linewidth=0.2, colour="red", linetype = "dashed")+
  coord_fixed(ratio = 0.3)+
  theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
Fig4c
```

Is there a correlation between d34S and % marine consumption, by site? Pooling all
sites together gives essentially no correlation (r ~ 0, Fig5a) - but this masks a
positive within-site relationship at three of the four sites, because each site sits
in its own d34S/%marine cluster (Jab II close to 100% marine with little d34S spread;
Moraes/Piaçaguera/Morro do Ouro spanning a wider range) - pooling erases the trend
that holds *within* a site.

```{r}
humans_mix <- Result_mix_TP_final %>% filter(group == "Human", !is.na(Mean_marine), !is.na(d34S))
d34S_marine_by_site <- humans_mix %>% group_by(Site) %>% summarise(
  n = n(),
  r = ifelse(n() >= 3, cor(d34S, Mean_marine, method = "pearson"), NA),
  p = ifelse(n() >= 3, cor.test(d34S, Mean_marine, method = "pearson")$p.value, NA)
)
d34S_marine_by_site
cor.test(humans_mix$d34S, humans_mix$Mean_marine, method = "pearson")  # pooled, for comparison
```
